overview: Samoa is an island country in the South Pacific. Its capital, Apia, is on the island of Upolu. In 1962 Samoa became the first Pacific island country to gain independence in the 20th century, from New Zealand. Traditional Samoan culture, called fa'a Samoa, remains strong, and rugby is very popular.

geography.text: Samoa is made up of two large volcanic islands, Savai'i and Upolu, and several small ones. The islands rise to mountains in the centre, with rainforest, waterfalls and old lava fields, and are ringed by coral reefs and beaches.

history.text: Samoa was settled about 3,000 years ago. In 1899 the islands were divided: the western part became German and the eastern part American, today American Samoa. New Zealand took over Western Samoa in 1914, and it became independent in 1962. In 2011 Samoa moved to the other side of the International Date Line, skipping 30 December.

events.title: Islands divided
events.text: Germany and the United States divide Samoa.

events.title: Black Saturday
events.text: New Zealand police fire on a peaceful independence march.

events.title: Date line moved
events.text: Samoa skips a day to move west of the date line.

government.text: Samoa is a parliamentary republic. Parliament elects the head of state, and the Prime Minister leads the government. Only matai, the chiefs of extended families, could be elected to parliament until recently and still dominate politics. In 2021 Fiamē Naomi Mataʻafa became its first female Prime Minister.

economy.text: Samoa's economy depends on money from Samoans abroad, tourism, farming and fishing. Coconut products and taro are exports.

culture.text: Fa'a Samoa, the Samoan way of life, centres on extended families and their matai, or chiefs. Traditional tattoos, called tatau, give the English word 'tattoo'. In 2011 Samoa moved west across the International Date Line, skipping 30 December.

items.title: Tatau
items.text: Traditional tattooing, the origin of the word 'tattoo'.

sport.text: Rugby union is the national sport, and the national team, Manu Samoa, has played at most Rugby World Cups. Many Samoans and people of Samoan heritage star in American football, rugby and wrestling.

items.title: Manu Samoa
items.text: Reached the Rugby World Cup quarter-finals in 1991 and 1995.

didYouKnow: In 2011 Samoa skipped 30 December to move west of the International Date Line.
The word 'tattoo' comes from the Samoan word 'tatau'.

keyPeople.name: Dwayne Johnson
keyPeople.text: Has Samoan heritage through his mother.
